'''Sabine Bögli''' (also published as Boegli) is a Swiss mathematician specialising in [[mathematical analysis]],
including the [[spectral theory]] of [[Self-adjoint operator|non-self-adjoint]]  [[Schrödinger operator]]s and their applications in [[mathematical physics]].{{r|whitehead}} Her research has resolved a decades-old dispute over the location of [[Autoionization|autoionizing resonances]] in atoms and molecules,{{r|whitehead|resonance|enclosure}} answered a longstanding open question on the accumulation of [[eigenvalue]]s of Schrödinger operators,{{r|whitehead|lapsaf}} and disproved a conjecture of Laptev and Safronov relating the magnitude of these eigenvalues to the norm of the potential.{{r|whitehead|lapsaf}} She works in England as an associate professor at [[Durham University]].{{r|profile}}

==Education and career==
Bögli is Swiss, and speaks [[Swiss German]] natively. After secondary education at the {{ill|Gymnasium Biel-Seeland|de}} in [[Biel/Bienne]], she studied mathematics at the [[University of Bern]], receiving a bachelor's degree in 2010, a master's degree in 2012, and a Ph.D. in 2014.{{r|cv}} Her doctoral dissertation, ''Spectral approximation for linear operators and applications'', was supervised by [[Christiane Tretter]].{{r|cv|mg}}

After postdoctoral research at the University of Bern, [[Cardiff University]], [[Imperial College London]], and [[LMU Munich]], and a Chapman Fellowship at Imperial College London, she joined [[Durham University]] as an assistant professor in 2019. She was promoted to associate professor in 2023.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Bögli was a 2024 recipient of the [[Whitehead Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]], given for her research on Schrödinger operators.{{r|whitehead|whitehead2}}
